_schema._description: Comprehension quizzes keyed by scene ID. When a student arrives at that scene, the quiz appears. Each has 4 options, one correct, plus an explanation shown after answering.
_schema._note: Quizzes are keyed to scene IDs from scenes.json. Add or remove freely — only scenes with matching keys will show a quiz.

creon_returns.q: What did the oracle of Apollo say?
options: The plague will end if Thebes builds a temple
The killer of Laius is hiding in Thebes
creon_returns.explain: Apollo said a killer remains in the city — and the plague will not end until he is found.

tiresias_accuses.explain: Scelus means 'crime'. Tiresias accuses Oedipus directly — a huge moment in the play.

iocasta_truth.q: Why does Jocasta think oracles are false?
options: Because her baby died — so the prophecy didn't happen
Because Apollo never spoke to her
iocasta_truth.explain: She believes her baby died on the mountain, so the prophecy that 'her son will kill his father' couldn't have come true. She is wrong.

messenger_reveal.q: Who actually gave baby Oedipus to the messenger?
messenger_reveal.explain: The shepherd handed the baby to the Corinthian messenger on the mountain. The chain of evidence is closing.

ending.q: Why does Oedipus say he was 'blind' before, but now will 'truly see'?
options: Because he could see with his eyes but not the truth — now he sees the truth
ending.explain: The whole tragedy turns on this: Oedipus had perfect eyes but was blind to the truth. Tiresias was blind in the eyes but saw everything. The play's central image.

tiresias_scene.q: Tiresias says 'noli quaerere' — what does this mean?
tiresias_scene.explain: Noli + infinitive is the standard way to say 'do not...' in Latin. Quaerere = 'to ask / to seek'. Tiresias is warning Oedipus to stop investigating.

pastor_speaks.q: What does the shepherd reveal about Oedipus?
options: Oedipus was actually born in Corinth
Oedipus is the son of Laius and Jocasta — not the son of Polybus
Oedipus was the one who fled the crossroads
pastor_speaks.explain: The shepherd was given the baby by Jocasta to leave on the mountain — but he saved the baby and gave it to the Corinthian messenger. The 'son of Corinth' is really the son of Thebes.

reckoning.q: Which choice reflects the canonical Sophocles ending — the one most readers expect?
options: Blind yourself and accept the gods' justice
Pronounce your own exile and save Thebes
reckoning.explain: In Sophocles, Oedipus blinds himself when the truth is revealed and asks to be exiled. The other three branches here are 'what-ifs' that explore the same fate from different character flaws.
